newsitem.title: FRANCE: LVMH says finalised DFS deal.
newsitem.headline: LVMH says finalised DFS deal.

text.p: LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton said on Saturday that it had finalised the acquisition of a 58.75 percent stake in U.S. duty free store chain DFS after U.S. anti-trust authorities cleared the purchase by LVMH of a remaining 8.85 percent stake in one of the companies owned by DFS.

"Federal anti-trust authorities have approved the acquisition by LVMH of an outstanding 8.85 percent tranche in one of the companies of the DFS group. As a result of that approval, the transfer of titles and related payments were made," the company said in a statement.
In December a U.S. arbitrator gave DFS shareholders the green light to sell 58.75 percent of DFS to LVMH despite the opposition of minority shareholders.
LVMH said at the time that completion of the $2.47 billion deal hinged on clearance from the U.S. Federal Trade Commission examining anti-trust implications.
In the statement LVMH reiterated that thanks to the acquisition its turnover will increase by close to 50 percent and operating results by around 30 percent.
News that U.S. authorities had cleared the deal came as two DFS shareholders on Friday said they were seeking to reverse the U.S. arbitrator decision permitting the sale.
Robert Miller and Anthony Pilaro shareholders with a 41.25 percent stake in DFS filed a motion with the Supreme Court of the State of New York seeking to vacate the deal.
They said Ira Millstein, the independent arbitrator, did not give them opportunity to present evidence of an inherent conflict of interest between LVMH and DFS.
They also alleged that LVMH would show no concern for the interests of DFS minority shareholders.
An LVMH spokeswoman reached by Reuters declined to comment.
